Global rate hike fears resurface even as equities rally
Global stocks staged a strong recovery led by technology shares, giving the S&P 500 its best week since April 2025, but the rally sits uneasily alongside core inflation in the United States climbing to 3.3 percent. That reading has revived expectations that the Federal Reserve may need to hike rates again, keeping bond yields and the dollar elevated and limiting the upside for emerging-market assets including Indian equities 530075361655290544725387355342.

China’s aggressive stimulus provides a powerful but uncertain tailwind
Chinese equities recorded their largest gain in over two years after Beijing issued a rare midday statement vowing stronger market support and mobilising state investors to buy shares. While the surge lifted sentiment across Asia, the durability of the rally depends on whether policy moves translate into sustained earnings improvement rather than a one-off sentiment boost 537735529355299.

United States trade pressure on India intensifies alongside trade deal progress
President Trump proposed new tariffs targeting 14 nations including India and Vietnam, aiming to redirect global trade away from China, even as India–United States negotiations near finalisation with Washington offering a 17 percent tariff cap. The simultaneous escalation and negotiation create a binary outcome for export-oriented sectors: a deal could lock in preferential access, while failure would expose Indian goods to steep duties 544765364255328531185470555218.

Domestic inflation breaches the Reserve Bank’s tolerance band, complicating monetary easing
Retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent in October, driven by food prices and festive demand, pushing it above the Reserve Bank of India’s 6 percent upper limit. Although the World Bank upgraded India’s FY27 growth forecast to 7.1 percent and the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent with a neutral stance, the inflation overshoot reduces the probability of near-term rate cuts and keeps borrowing costs sticky for rate-sensitive sectors 5473754130551895413455142.

Record foreign inflows fail to prevent a market correction as crude oil spikes
Foreign institutional investors pumped a massive ₹1,29,579 crore into Indian equities in November, driving the Nifty 50 to an 11 percent monthly gain and pushing equity turnover to a six-month high. Yet the benchmark indices snapped a four-week winning streak, falling roughly 0.75 percent, as Brent crude climbed toward $97–98 per barrel, the rupee weakened, and bond yields spiked, creating a tug-of-war between abundant liquidity and deteriorating macro inputs 5422155351551915424954751538935412853098.

Banking system liquidity gets targeted relief while asset-quality risks accumulate in gold loans
The RBI reduced daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance to 90 percent effective 1 December, easing a deepening liquidity deficit and giving banks more room to lend. At the same time, falling bullion prices are triggering early delinquencies, higher margin calls, and auction risks in gold-backed loan portfolios, while drought conditions in Maharashtra and Karnataka threaten agricultural asset quality 554905460352961530965386253393533985386954578.

IT services face structural headwinds from United States visa curbs and AI-driven cost restructuring
IBM announced it will discontinue US visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles, requiring affected staff to relocate to India or exit by 31 December, while global majors such as SAP are reportedly planning cuts of at least 10,000 jobs as they pivot to generative AI. These moves shrink the traditional onsite staffing model that underpins Indian IT margins, even as select domestic firms like Persistent Systems and E2E Networks win large AI and cloud infrastructure orders 553335443653057545205498354736.

Market mood

Sentiment is caught between powerful cross-currents: record foreign buying and upgraded growth forecasts provide a solid floor, but sticky inflation, rising crude, and the spectre of US tariffs and Fed tightening cap the upside. Investors are likely to adopt a stock-specific, quality-biased approach while watching the 26,000–26,300 resistance zone on the Nifty for direction.

tabs.one: NSE briefly becomes the world's 3rd largest stock exchange, while Swiggy Instamart cuts 340 jobs amid intensifying quick commerce competition and AI automation.
tabs.html:
The big stories

  • NSE Milestone: India’s National Stock Exchange (NSE) briefly emerged as the world's 3rd largest stock exchange operator by market cap, overtaking the London Stock Exchange Group and Germany’s Deutsche Boerse as its shares surged 3.5% 46.
  • Swiggy Instamart Layoffs: Swiggy's quick commerce arm laid off 340 corporate and support staff as it faces mounting losses and fierce competition, leaning further into AI automation 128.
  • WhatsApp & CERT-In Warnings: CERT-In issued a high-severity security advisory for WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business across Android, iOS, and desktop, warning that vulnerabilities could allow remote code execution 130. Meanwhile, WhatsApp announced a new Travel eSIM feature allowing users to buy international data plans in-app, partnering with Reliance Jio and others 104.
  • Jio Platform Moves: Reliance's Jio Platforms quickly took down its newly launched AI astrology platform, JioAstro, just hours after its public rollout 49.
  • Enterprise Tech Deals: Wipro secured a massive contract valued at over $500 million (approx. ₹4,700 crore) with British energy major BP to manage core finance operations, absorbing around 3,000 BP employees 41.

Launches & products

  • HP OmniBook Ultra 16: Launched in India at ₹5,49,999, featuring the Nvidia RTX Spark N1X platform for high-performance on-device AI workloads 51.
  • Instagram for TV: Meta launched Instagram for TV in India, bringing Reels and creator content to Apple TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Google TV 108.
  • Insta360 Ace Pro 3: Teased for a December 1 launch with variable aperture, autofocus, and interchangeable lenses 106.
  • Anthropic 'Install as app': A new beta feature allowing users to convert Claude Artifacts into standalone Windows and macOS desktop applications 43.

The market angle

  • National Stock Exchange (NSE): Shares surged 3.5% as it briefly hit the world's #3 spot by market capitalization 46.
  • Wipro: Landed a major ₹4,700 crore ($500M+) deal with BP to take over core finance operations and absorb 3,000 employees 41.
  • Reliance Industries / Jio: Partnered via Jio for WhatsApp’s new in-app Travel eSIM feature 104, while hastily pulling its newly launched JioAstro AI platform offline 49.
  • Swiggy: Quick commerce unit Swiggy Instamart trimmed 340 jobs amid ongoing financial losses and competitive pressure 128.
  • Adani Group: CFO Jugeshinder Singh confirmed the conglomerate's interest in entering India's airline market via a stake acquisition or funding new operators 40.

Worth reading

  • 14 Nasscom highlights how AI could traditionalise and shrink IT maintenance and call centre markets while opening new software development cost efficiencies for Indian tech.
